ov: The larval stage of butterflies and moths, built for eating and growing. Most eat leaves and are serious farm pests, though about 1% eat insects. They defend themselves with camouflage, warning colours, toxins taken from plants and, in some species, stinging hairs.

why.dg: Some have venomous hairs: the South American Lonomia caterpillar’s venom can cause fatal bleeding in humans.

df: Mostly plant material, often leaves; some eat insects, and clothes moths eat wool.
fx: A tobacco hornworm increases its weight ten-thousandfold in less than 20 days.
Monarch caterpillars store poisons from their food plants and keep them as adults.
